newsitem.title: ESTONIA: C.BANK HEAD SAYS GDP IN LINE WITH FORECASTS.
newsitem.headline: C.BANK HEAD SAYS GDP IN LINE WITH FORECASTS.

text.p: Estonia's central bank governor Vahur Kraft said on Friday that economic growth was in line with forecasts for 1997.
In an interview with Reuters, Kraft said the Bank of Estonia forecast Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth for the year at a little above four percent and inflation at about 15 percent.
"I think we are line with the forecasts we have," Kraft said.
"Maybe in some cases our forecasts are little bit lower than others.
"But the central bank will always be quite conservative because we need to give the economy the right signals, ones that don't build up too big hopes."
The central bank forecast GDP growth in 1995 at three percent and it came in at 4.5 percent.
"It is a bit hard to forecast in this open and quite fast moving economy," Kraft said.
He said the latest Consumer Price Index figures showing a 0.9 percent rise in February showed inflation was in line with forecasts.
In coming years Kraft expected the rate of decline in inflation to slow.
"We see a lowering of the inflation speed but we are not able to say concrete figures," he said.
"Overall our forecasts are that over two or three years our inflation will be lower than 10 percent and the average of GDP growth will be around four or five percent on average."
